Then run the §11.7 regression coverage plan (backfill_test.exs fail-then-pass, one more instance, tenant_fixture_dispatch_test.exs's :replay branch, the async:true isolation test, and as much of TEST-RUNNER's originally-reported 18-19 failing files as practical) before routing to SECURITY-REVIEWER/REVIEWER. result.summary:
Implemented §11.1/§11.2/§11.3/§11.6's dispatch mechanism exactly as specified in test/support/data_case.ex and test/support/tenant_fixture.ex, then found a real, reproducible contradiction inside the design itself while running the §11.7-required regression plan -- reported as a BLOCKER per this handoff's own instruction, not patched around.

WHAT WAS IMPLEMENTED (compiles clean, formatted clean):

1. test/support/data_case.ex: added `Process.put(:letflow_data_case_shared_mode?, !tags[:async])` immediately after the existing `unless tags[:async] do ... end` block, exactly per §11.1/§11.6 item 1. No other line changed.

2. test/support/tenant_fixture.ex: added a new private `provision_via_shared_connection/1` (mirrors `with_provisioning_repo/1`'s `(fun :: (-> result)) :: result` shape, no @spec, matching that function's own unspecced precedent) implementing §11.2's steps: `Repo.put_dynamic_repo(Letflow.Repo)` (stated explicitly, not assumed), run `fun.()`, restore the previous dynamic repo in an `after` block -- and, critically, it issues NO Sandbox.mode/2 call of any kind, matching §11.2 step 3's load-bearing property. `provisioned_tenant!/1`'s body now computes `template = Keyword.get(opts, :template, :clone)` and picks `connection_wrap = if template == :clone and Process.get(:letflow_data_case_shared_mode?, false), do: &provision_via_shared_connection/1, else: &with_provisioning_repo/1` -- exactly §11.1's dispatch rule plus §11.2.1's `template: :replay` override. The `on_exit/1` teardown registration was changed from the old unconditional `with_provisioning_repo(fn -> teardown(...) end)` to `connection_wrap.(fn -> teardown(...) end)`, so provisioning and teardown for the same call always share one dispatch decision, per §11.3. `opts()`'s type, `provisioned_tenant!/1`'s public @spec, and `tenant_fixture()`'s return shape are byte-for-byte unchanged. Moduledoc updated per §11.6 item 2's last bullet to state the dual-path dispatch and cite design §11 alongside §10.

`mix compile --warnings-as-errors --force`: clean, 190 files, zero warnings. `mix format --check-formatted`: clean, no output.

THE BLOCKER, found by running §11.7's own required fail-then-pass check on backfill_test.exs:

Pre-fix (git stash to isolate; §10-only code, no §11 dispatch): `mix test test/letflow/tenant_provisioning/backfill_test.exs` -> `Result: 4/5 passed`, 1 failure, the exact documented ISS-0332 symptom (`assert updated >= 1` / `left: 0` / `right: 1`) -- matches §11.7 item 1's expected pre-fix red exactly.

Post-fix (git stash pop, my §11 implementation applied): the SAME command now returns `Result: 0/5 passed` -- WORSE than pre-fix, not fixed. All 5 tests fail with an identical new symptom: `clone_tenant_schema!/1 returned {:error, {:clone_failed, %Ecto.InvalidChangesetError{... errors: [tenant_id: {"does not exist", [constraint: :foreign, constraint_name: "tenant_schemas_tenant_id_fkey"]}] ...}}}`.

ROOT CAUSE, traced to source, not guessed: `test/support/tenant_template.ex:82`, inside `Letflow.Test.TenantTemplate.ensure_template!/0` (called by `provision_schema!(:clone, tenant_id)`, which EVERY default-template caller goes through, async or not): `Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto)`, issued UNCONDITIONALLY, as that function's own first line, targeting the LITERAL `Letflow.Repo` module (not through any dynamic-repo indirection). Design §9.7 already documented this exact call site (quoted verbatim, 'confirmed by direct read ... that ensure_template!/0 calls Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto) unconditionally, as its own first line') and concluded from it that ':auto mode is not something either template path could be made to avoid needing' -- correct advice for the §10 world, where EVERY caller's provisioning ran on ProvisioningRepo and Letflow.Repo's own mode was irrelevant to provisioning. But §11.2 now routes an async:false + template::clone caller's OWN Tenant insert and clone_tenant_schema!/1 call onto Letflow.Repo directly (via `provision_via_shared_connection/1`'s `put_dynamic_repo(Letflow.Repo)`), while relying on its own single load-bearing property that this path 'issues zero Sandbox.mode/2 calls of any kind' (§11.2 step 3, §11.4's first bullet). That property is FALSE for the :clone path: `ensure_template!/0`'s own unconditional `Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto)` call still fires, on the SAME Letflow.Repo the caller's own connection is checked out from under {:shared, self()} mode. Per §9.1's own no-op-only-on-same-mode guard (already normative, quoted throughout §9-§11), a mode change from {:shared, self()} to :auto is NOT a no-op -- it is a real, disruptive, global check-in of every currently-checked-out Letflow.Repo connection, including the caller's own in-flight Tenant-insert transaction. That is exactly Mechanism 4 (§9.2), reintroduced by a call site §11 never audited, on the exact population (async:false, :clone-path, the default combination for 44 of 47 real callers) §11 exists to fix. The caller's own Tenant row is checked in and rolled back before clone_tenant_schema!/1's FK check runs against it -- hence the fkey violation on literally every :clone-path async:false test, a strictly worse outcome than the pre-§11 (§10-only) baseline.

WHY THIS IS A DESIGN CONTRADICTION, NOT AN IMPLEMENTATION BUG: §11.2's own text states its single load-bearing property as absolute ('no Sandbox.mode/2 call of any kind, anywhere in this function' -- referring to the whole provisioning sequence this function drives, not merely its own body's literal statements, per §11.2 step 2's own framing that provision_schema!/2's existing functions run 'exactly as with_provisioning_repo/1's own body already sequences them'). §11.2.1 exhaustively re-verified this against `Ecto.Migrator.run/4`'s two-connection requirement for the :clone-vs-:replay question, and correctly found :clone 'does not call Ecto.Migrator.run/4 at all' -- but never checked whether the :clone path makes its OWN Sandbox.mode/2 call independent of the migrator question. It does, via `ensure_template!/0`, and §9.7 (written for a different, now-superseded routing world) is the section that already documented this same call site without anyone connecting the two. §11.4's own re-verification pass ('does dispatching on template: :replay reopen anything? ... there is no third mechanism to separately verify') explicitly asserts there are only two Sandbox.mode/2-calling code paths in the whole design (ProvisioningRepo's, and §11.2's own zero-call path) -- that assertion is what is false; ensure_template!/0 is a third, pre-existing one that fires unconditionally on the :clone path regardless of which of §11's two dispatch branches is chosen, and §11 nowhere states what should happen to it.

WHAT I DID NOT DO: I did not invent a fix (e.g. wrapping ensure_template!/0's own call in the dynamic-repo indirection, or making it repo-parameterized, or skipping it when already-built) because any of those is a real mechanism decision -- which repo ensure_template!/0's own :auto call should target when called from the shared-connection path, and whether that call's own global check-in effect (even if retargeted) is safe under §11's dispatch -- that CODE-DESIGNER, not ELIXIR-DEV, must make and CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR must gate, per this project's design/implementation split and this handoff's own explicit instruction to stop rather than guess on a genuine design ambiguity/contradiction.

CURRENT STATE OF THE WORKING TREE: my §11.1/§11.2/§11.3/§11.6 implementation (data_case.ex, tenant_fixture.ex) is left IN PLACE, uncommitted, exactly as described above -- it correctly implements everything §11 explicitly specifies; the gap is something §11 does not specify at all. No commit was made. TEST-RUNNER's originally-reported 18-19 failing files were not run at scope per §11.7 item 4, because the backfill_test.exs check (item 1, required first) surfaced this BLOCKER before that broader run could produce meaningful signal -- running it now would mix genuine §11-mechanism confirmation with this newly-introduced regression and produce a noisy, unusable report. tenant_fixture_dispatch_test.exs and the async:true isolation test were likewise not yet re-run for the same reason (both also exercise :clone-path provisioning and would show the same new symptom for any async:false case they cover, muddying the signal for what is actually a narrow, well-understood gap).

issues.description: Design §11.2/§11.4's load-bearing safety property ('provision_via_shared_connection/1's path issues zero Sandbox.mode/2 calls of any kind, on any repo') is false for the default template: :clone path: test/support/tenant_template.ex:82's Letflow.Test.TenantTemplate.ensure_template!/0 issues an unconditional Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto) call as its own first line, on every :clone-path invocation, already documented by this same design's own §9.7 for a different (now-superseded) routing context but never reconciled against §11's own claim that only two Sandbox.mode/2-calling paths exist. Reproduced directly: mix test test/letflow/tenant_provisioning/backfill_test.exs goes from 4/5 passed (pre-fix, matching §11.7's expected red) to 0/5 passed (post-fix, all 5 failing on Ecto.InvalidChangesetError / tenant_schemas_tenant_id_fkey does not exist) once §11's dispatch is implemented exactly as specified -- a regression strictly worse than the bug §11 exists to fix, on the exact population (44 of 47 real callers) §11 targets. CODE-DESIGNER must decide and state explicitly what ensure_template!/0's own Sandbox.mode/2 call should do under the async:false/shared-connection dispatch path (candidates include, but this handoff does not choose among them: routing ensure_template!/0's own call through the same dynamic-repo binding provision_via_shared_connection/1 established so it targets whichever repo is currently dynamic rather than Letflow.Repo literally; skipping the call entirely when template_ready?/0 is already true and the caller is on the shared-connection path; or some other mechanism this design has not yet considered) -- and CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR must re-gate that decision before ELIXIR-DEV resumes.

result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGNER for a targeted §11 rework (iteration 3) addressing ensure_template!/0's own unconditional Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto) call under the async:false/template::clone dispatch path, then CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR re-gate, then back to ELIXIR-DEV to finish implementation (the data_case.ex and tenant_fixture.ex edits already made for §11.1/§11.2/§11.3/§11.6 stay valid and should not be re-done, only extended) and complete the §11.7 regression plan and full-suite verification.
